rv.q: Not an ounce of “great theatre” stiffness here: this is raw, poetic, painful and plausible.
Paul Mescal is terrifying and Patsy Ferran is unbelievably good in Rebecca Frecknall’s thrillingly dissonant revival of Tennessee Williams’s masterpiece
The final scene, which shows forceful restraint being applied to the carted-away heroine is heart-stopping.
On a few occasions, Rebecca Frecknell’s production feels over stylised.

cn.t: Critics praise Rebecca Frecknall's revival as thrilling, with Paul Mescal delivering a tremendous Stanley Kowalski and Patsy Ferran earning sensational notices as Blanche DuBois.

vr.q: it was such a thrilling piece of theater there were so many wonderful elements of it and such fantastic performances that I simply wouldn't be rest if I didn't come on here and tell you how much I enjoyed it
